blocks.x: Agent-fleet management run like workforce management: capacity plans against demand curves, shift and version discipline, credential rotation, utilization that is measured honestly — and SLAs that hold while the fleet upgrades underneath the business.
Fifty agents are a workforce, and workforces need management

Once you have a dozen agents, you have a workforce — and workforces need management. Capacity planning against demand curves, version upgrades without breaking in-flight work, retirement of agents whose roles have changed, utilization measurement that is honest about idle time.

The orchestration layer is the missing middle between 'we built an agent' and 'the agent fleet runs the operation': scheduling, load balancing across agent versions, credential rotation fleets-wide, and the discipline to retire agents instead of letting them become furniture.
Below: the failure modes that grow fleets into liabilities, the reference architecture of the fleet layer, and the console that runs the digital workforce like the human one.
Four ways fleets sprawl into liabilities
Each failure mode is an HR problem wearing a DevOps costume — the countermeasures borrow deliberately from workforce management practice.

widgets.title: Utilization by agent class × daypart — find the idle specialists
widgets.note: Hover cells to read exact utilization. The 22–06 column is the staffing argument: either route deferred work to night-capable classes or stop paying for idle specialists overnight.

widgets.title: Identity posture what-if — rotation and scope audit intervals
widgets.note: The hygiene curve makes the cost of lazy rotation visible: an agent with 90-day credential rotation is a standing finding, and the score shows exactly where the CISO's line sits.

widgets.title: Handoff topology — click a lane node to see its contract

nodes.label: Task router
nodes.detail: Routes by capability registry and current load; every routing decision is logged with the candidates it rejected, so misroutes are debuggable.

nodes.label: Document agents
nodes.detail: Class-scoped specialists; they may not hand work sideways to each other — lateral handoffs bypass review and are denied by policy.

nodes.label: Data agents
nodes.detail: Own typed reads/writes; every write idempotent, every read cached by content hash for cost.

nodes.label: QA critics
nodes.detail: Verify outputs against class assertions; a failed assertion returns the work with machine-readable reasons, not a vague rejection.

nodes.label: Escalation desk
nodes.detail: Bundles evidence packets for human review; the packet is the contract — no context-free "please check this".

nodes.label: Human queue
nodes.detail: Reviewers with SLAs; their overrides feed the routing model weekly — the fleet learns from every correction.

widgets.note: Sideways handoffs are denied by policy; the graph is deliberately hierarchical so every output passes exactly one critic.
